prompt: Company profile: Scrap metal recycler in Pasadena, Texas; 35 employees. Situation: The company is opening a new 4-acre outdoor yard for receiving, sorting, shearing, and staging ferrous and nonferrous scrap. Rainfall runs off the yard to a municipal storm drain. Texas (TCEQ) administers the NPDES program (TPDES). Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
**Compliance Obligations Register – New 4‑acre Outdoor Scrap Yard** *Pasadena, Texas – 35‑employee scrap metal recycler* --- ### 1. TPDES Industrial Stormwater General Permit (TXR050000) – Sector N (Scrap Recycling) | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Requirement** | Obtain permit coverage; develop and certify a site‑specific Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWP3); install, maintain, and inspect best management practices (BMPs); conduct benchmark monitoring; submit an annual report and Discharge Monitoring Reports (DMRs). | | **Source** | Texas Water Code § 26.027; 30 TAC Chapters 281, 305; TCEQ General Permit TXR050000 (Part V, Sector N – Scrap Recycling Facilities). | | **Applicability to this company** | Directly applicable. The 4‑acre outdoor yard is an “industrial facility” with activities (receiving, sorting, shearing, staging) that expose pollutants to stormwater, which discharges to a municipal storm drain. No‑exclusion certification is not feasible because materials are stored outdoors. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Direct** – The permit is a legal requirement that relates to the organization’s environmental aspects (stormwater pollution). | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Indirect** – BMPs and spill‑prevention measures also reduce slip/trip hazards and exposure to harmful substances, linking to OH&S operational controls. | | **How / When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | • **Method:** Review of permit coverage letter, SWP3 implementation records, BMP inspection logs, DMRs, and benchmark monitoring data.
• **Frequency:** **Quarterly** internal compliance audits (permit conditions, BMP functionality); **monthly** visual inspections of BMPs; **annual** third‑party sampling for benchmark parameters; **annual** management review of the permit status and any TCEQ correspondence. | --- ### 2. Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWP3) | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Requirement** | Prepare a written SWP3 that identifies potential pollutant sources, selects appropriate BMPs (structural & non‑structural), maps discharge points, and includes employee‑training procedures. The SWP3 must be kept on‑site and updated whenever operations change. | | **Source** | Required by TCEQ General Permit TXR050000, Part III; EPA “Developing Your Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan” guidance. | | **Applicability to this company** | Directly applicable. The new yard constitutes a “new industrial activity” that must be covered before discharge begins. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Direct** – The SWP3 is a legal document that operationalizes compliance obligations. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Indirect** – Spill‑response and housekeeping procedures within the SWP3 also protect workers from chemical and physical hazards. | | **How / When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | • **Method:** Document review, field verification of BMPs, training records.
• **Frequency:** **Before** first discharge; **annually** thereafter (or after any significant change); **quarterly** internal audits of BMP implementation. | --- ### 3. Benchmark Monitoring & Annual Reporting | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Requirement** | Collect stormwater samples from each outfall during a qualifying rain event; analyze for benchmark parameters (e.g., TSS, pH, oil & grease, copper, lead, zinc). Submit an annual report (DMRs) to TCEQ by March 31 each year. | | **Source** | TXR050000, Part V; 30 TAC § 281.25. | | **Applicability to this company** | Directly applicable. Scrap recycling is a “benchmark” sector under the general permit. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Direct** – Monitoring and reporting are legal requirements tied to the environmental aspect. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Not directly applicable** – No immediate OH&S legal nexus, but data may inform spill‑response safety. | | **How / When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | • **Method:** Review laboratory results, DMR submittal confirmations, TCEQ feedback.
• **Frequency:** **Quarterly** review of monitoring data for trends; **annual** submission verification; **monthly** check of sampling equipment and chain‑of‑custody records. | --- ### 4. Best Management Practices (BMPs) – Installation & Maintenance | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Requirement** | Install structural BMPs (e.g., silt fences, detention basins, oil‑water separators) and non‑structural BMPs (e.g., good housekeeping, spill kits, employee training). Maintain BMPs in effective operating condition. | | **Source** | TXR050000, Part III; SWP3 requirements. | | **Applicability to this company** | Directly applicable. The yard’s 4‑acre impervious/partially‑impervious surface will generate runoff that must be treated or controlled. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Direct** – BMPs are operational controls required by law. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Direct** – Proper BMP maintenance reduces slip hazards, equipment collisions, and exposure to sharp or contaminated materials. | | **How / When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | • **Method:** Visual inspections, maintenance logs, employee interview/training records.
• **Frequency:** **Weekly** site inspections (housekeeping, spill‑kit readiness); **monthly** structural BMP maintenance checks; **quarterly** internal audit of BMP effectiveness. | --- ### 5. City of Pasadena Municipal Stormwater Ordinance (MS4 Program) | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Requirement** | Comply with local discharge prohibitions, reporting of illicit discharges, and any city‑specific BMP or inspection requirements. May require a local industrial discharge permit or registration with the city’s Public Works Department. | | **Source** | Pasadena Code of Ordinances (e.g., Chapter 26 – Stormwater Management); City’s MS4 Permit (if applicable). | | **Applicability to this company** | Directly applicable. Discharge enters a municipal storm drain that is part of the city’s MS4 system; the city may impose stricter controls than TCEQ. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Direct** – Municipal requirements are “other legal requirements.” | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Indirect** – Local safety ordinances (e.g., traffic control, dust control) may overlap. | | **How / When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | • **Method:** Review city permit/registration, correspondence with Public Works, inspection reports.
• **Frequency:** **Annual** review of ordinance updates; **quarterly** coordination with city inspectors; **monthly** verification of local BMPs (e.g., street sweeping, inlet protection). | --- ### 6. Construction General Permit (TXR150000) – If Construction Disturbs >1 Acre | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Requirement** | Obtain TCEQ Construction General Permit coverage; develop a construction‑phase SWP3; install erosion and sediment controls; conduct weekly inspections; stabilize the site upon completion. | | **Source** | 30 TAC Chapter 281; TCEQ General Permit TXR150000. | | **Applicability to this company** | **Conditionally applicable** – If the 4‑acre yard is being **newly constructed** (grading, paving, building installation) and disturbs >1 acre, this permit is required **before** ground‑breaking. If the yard is already built, this obligation is historical. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Direct** (if applicable) – Construction‑phase stormwater control is a legal requirement. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Direct** – Construction activities introduce OH&S hazards (excavation, equipment, dust). | | **How / When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | • **Method:** Inspection logs, stabilization photos, permit termination letter.
• **Frequency:** **Weekly** during active construction; **final** inspection after stabilization; **annual** review if permit is still active. | --- ### 7. Spill Prevention, Control & Countermeasure (SPCC) Plan | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Requirement** | If the facility stores petroleum products (e.g., diesel fuel for shears, lubricants) in aboveground tanks **≥1,320 gal aggregate** or underground tanks **≥42,000 gal**, prepare and implement an SPCC Plan. | | **Source** | 40 CFR 112; 30 TAC Chapter 327. | | **Applicability to this company** | **Conditionally applicable** – Assess total petroleum storage capacity. Most scrap yards with heavy equipment exceed the 1,320‑gal threshold. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Direct** – SPCC is a federal/state environmental requirement. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Direct** – Spill prevention and response directly protect workers from fire, slip, and exposure hazards. | | **How / When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | • **Method:** Review SPCC Plan, tank inspection records, spill‑response drill logs, training records.
• **Frequency:** **Annual** plan review and certification; **monthly** tank inspections; **quarterly** spill‑response drills. | --- ### 8. OSHA General Industry Standards (29 CFR 1910) – Machine Guarding, LOTO, PPE | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Requirement** | Ensure shears, conveyors, and other machinery have proper guards; implement lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures; provide and enforce use of personal protective equipment (PPE). | | **Source** | 29 CFR 1910 Subparts O, S, and others; OSHA Hazard Communication Standard. | | **Applicability to this company** | Directly applicable. Shearing and sorting operations present amputation, struck‑by, and noise hazards. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Not directly applicable** – Primarily an OH&S legal requirement. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Direct** – OSHA standards are core legal OH&S obligations. | | **How / When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | • **Method:** Workplace inspections, LOTO audits, PPE compliance checks, incident/ near‑miss analysis.
• **Frequency:** **Monthly** safety inspections; **annual** LOTO audit; **quarterly** PPE inventory and training verification; **ongoing** incident investigation. | --- ### 9. Texas Hazard Communication Act (THCA) | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Requirement** | Maintain safety data sheets (SDS) for all hazardous chemicals (e.g., cutting fluids, solvents); provide employee training; ensure proper labeling. | | **Source** | Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 502; 25 TAC Chapter 296. | | **Applicability to this company** | Directly applicable if hazardous chemicals are used or stored on‑site. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Indirect** – Chemical management affects environmental aspects (spills, waste). | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Direct** – THCA is a legal OH&S requirement. | | **How / When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | • **Method:** SDS inventory audit, training records review, labeling inspections.
• **Frequency:** **Annual** training; **quarterly** SDS/labelling checks; **monthly** chemical storage inspections. | --- ### Summary of Evaluation Approach (ISO 9.1.2) For each obligation above, the organization must: 1. **Plan** – Document the compliance evaluation method, responsibility, and frequency in the EMS/OH&S management system procedures. 2. **Monitor** – Use a combination of inspections, audits, data review, and regulatory correspondence to gather objective evidence. 3. **Analyze** – Compare findings against legal and other requirements; identify non‑conformities and trends. 4. **Report** – Summarize compliance status during management review (minimum annually) and communicate results to relevant stakeholders. 5. **Retain** – Keep records of evaluations (e.g., audit reports, inspection logs, DMRs, training records) for the duration specified by the permit or standard (typically 3–5 years). By systematically registering and evaluating these obligations, the company ensures that the new Pasadena yard meets both environmental and occupational health & safety legal requirements while aligning with ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 management system expectations.
